assumptions: A1: a flat memory of at least 2^133.86 bytes addressed with 128-bit addresses; each 64-bit word access to the arrays above 2^64 bytes is charged 2 instructions, applying the cost model rule that larger data structures account for their implementation. Memory carries no score.

A2: the protected reference unit (batched incomplete affine G1 addition, 6M, C = 2000) prices each chain step; all other work is an itemised analytic worst-case instruction count, not machine code or a measurement.
limitations: No full-size run; the toy experiment checks the algorithm and the counting formulas exhaustively at toy scale only. Production success follows from the exact counting argument, not from the toy.
Success probability is exactly (g(2m+1)+1)/r, just above 0.40; the algorithm is deterministic and uses no coins.
preprocessing_log2 (126.83, rounded up) is the Q-independent baby phase, 2^126.8298 units, included in the total and not amortised.
Memory of 2^133.8516 bytes (memory_log2_bytes 133.86 rounded up) is physically unrealistic; only negation symmetry is used.
The algorithm has no random walk, hash, distinguished points or scalar accumulators.
